texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, on 09.06.2020, concerned police official reached the spot of accident Maa Anandmay Marg, near Courtesy Honda Red Light, Okhla Ind. Area from ESI hospital to Crown Plaza side. They found a person lying in the middle of the road and lots of blood already oozed out from his body and about 30-35 feet away offending car bearing no. DL-1CP-5871 Ritz white colour was found in standing condition. The front left side tyre of such car was found burst and front side glass was also damaged and there was skid marks about 8-10 feets on the road. No eye witness could be found at that time, but later on alleged eye witness/complainant Rajender Gaur's statement was got recorded. He stated that he alongwith victim Rajesh Kumar in the morning came for a walk at about 4.30 am at the spot of accident. MACT No. 356/21 Neelam v. Mushraf Ansari Page No 2 of 27 BK :3: Such Rajesh Kumar was walking about 10-15 steps in front of such complainant. At this time, one vehicle came in a very rash and negligent manner at a fast speed and took a right cut and hit the victim Rajesh Kumar. As a result, Rajesh Kumar stuck in right wheel of such vehicle and was dragged on the road and as a result Rajesh Kumar head bursted. He further stated that he shouted driver of the offending vehicle to stop but driver of the car did not stop. He further stated that after about 30-35 feet left side of the car got bursted and as a result driver came out of the car and got frightened after seeing the condition of Rajesh Kumar and he run away from the spot after leaving car at the spot. Such Rajender Gaur also stated that he can identify the driver of such offending vehicle if shown to him. Such, Rajender Gaur further claimed that he also got afraid and came to the village/his place of residence in Delhi to intimate other known people. He further stated that in the meanwhile, police took Rajesh Kumar/victim to the hospital. Accordingly, the FIR in question was recorded u/s 279,304A IPC. 3. Further, it was found that there was no third party Smt. Neelam (Wife) vs Mushraf Ansari on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172713701/ 2 insurance of such offending vehicle. 4. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence u/s 279,304A IPC & 146/196 MV Act against the respondent no.1/driver. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 5. Initially, R-1/driver and R-2/owner appeared with counsel in the present case but despite opportunity given, they failed to file any reply. MACT No. 356/21 Neelam v. Mushraf Ansari Page No 3 of 27 BK :4: 6. Further, my learned Predecessor issued a show- cause notice to R-1&R-2 for deposit of Rs.25 lacs as security in the form of FDR by the name of this Tribunal in view of provisions of MACT Rules as applicable to Delhi and directions by Hon'ble High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of uninsured vehicle. OPP 2. 8. Further, vide order dated 30.11.2022, it was noted that despite opportunity given, respondent failed to deposit the FDR of Rs.25 lacs as security. As such, their right to contest was closed. In fact, R-1&R-2 stopped appearing in the present proceedings. 9. Neelam/wife of deceased filed her examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/5 and Mark A and B including copy of death certificate, DAR and copy of Aadhar card. 10. Further, alleged eye witness/complainant Rajendra Gaud also examined as PW-2. He filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-2/A. 11 No other evidence has been led on behalf of MACT No. 356/21 Neelam v. Mushraf Ansari Page No 4 of 27 BK :5: petitioner. 12. Respondent side neither fulfilled the condition of deposit of security nor appeared as already noted above. But despite opportunity given, no arguments addressed by respondent side. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/304A of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.

Petitioner; Versus Pranay Sethi And Others (2017 Scc Online Sc 1270), decided by constitutional bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, regarding the concept of 'just compensation' it was held : "................55. Section 168 of the Act deals with the concept of "just compensation" and the same has to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability on acceptable legal standard because such determination can never be in arithmetical exactitude. It can never be perfect. The aim is to achieve an acceptable degree of proximity to arithmetical precision on the basis of materials brought on record in an individual case. The conception of "just compensation" has to be viewed through the prism of fairness, reasonableness and non-violation of the principle of equitability. Simultaneously, the compensation granted cannot be an apology for compensation. 25.
